attempts.label: DANDI:001517
attempts.paper_title: Sub-microsecond optical measurements of cell membrane charging and lesioning by pulsed electric fields
attempts.entry_title: Membrane charging and electroporation imaged with strobe fluorescence (Semenov et al. 2026)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Semenov, Silkuniene, Silkunas, Pakhomova, Bixler, Ibey, Kochunov and Pakhomov (2026) on dandiset 001517, which holds raw strobe images of CHO cells loaded with FluoVolt or Di-8-ANEPPS and exposed to 1-us pulses of escalating amplitude. Pole polarization, its decline within and across sets, the dye calibration against the Schwan equation and the departure from linear charging are rebuilt from the images. The Gd3+, 0.3-us, two-pulse, alternating-amplitude and Ca2+ experiments are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Semenov et al. (2026) from dandiset 001517

outcomes.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS and 1-us pulses, polarization grows with field strength up to 570 V/cm; at 780 V/cm the cathodic pole stops increasing and dims, and at 1000 to 1400 V/cm the poles show reduced or absent polarization while regions nearer the equator stay polarized and may polarize more than the poles.
outcomes.source: Figure 1 and its legend; Results 3.1, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: At a higher electric field strength of 780 V/cm, polarization at the cathodic pole does not further increase but dims out, indicating a less efficient charging of the partially permeabilized membrane. Still stronger electric fields produce a distinct pattern of reduced or absent polarization at the poles ... while regions closer to the equator remain relatively intact and may polarize more than the poles
outcomes.notes: Under every background reading the cathodic pole is lower at 780 than at 570 V/cm (far 38.6 against 41.7%; near 65.0 against 67.9; none 15.2 against 16.0), and at 1400 V/cm the largest mean dF of the cathode-facing hemisphere lies 65 degrees from the pole (far 21.7% at -65 degrees against 7.5% at the pole; near and none also at -65). Both conditions hold at every band of the background sweep and with the local backgrounds. In each of the 8 cells the 1400 V/cm maximum lies 43 to 76 degrees from the pole. Five-cell subsets passing 56 of 56 (far), 45 (near), 51 (none). The Fig. 1 cell is not identified; the test uses the Fig. 4B cells as the criterion says.
deviations: Field strengths are matched in order to the generator volts the files give (25 V as 43 V/cm, 50 as 150, 70 as 230, 100 as 360, 150 as 570, 200 as 780, 250 as 1000, 300 as 1200, 350 as 1400), an assumption. The paper names nine field strengths for its 1-us escalations and the files nine amplitudes, but the two are not proportional, and below electroporation the data fit a proportional response about as well on the volts as on the paper's V/cm. The first step supports the matching: from 25 to 50 V the mean pole |dF| triples (FluoVolt 3.05, Di-8-ANEPPS 2.90), against 3.49 for the paper's 43 to 150 V/cm and 2.00 for proportional volts. A variant with the field proportional to the volts (4 V/cm per V) is shown for every claim that uses the field strength as a number.

Background is subtracted from ROIs 30 to 36 pixels (8 to 10 um) outside the membrane, 20 degrees wide, near each pole (the far reading), an assumption. The paper does not state a background method for the laser images; its Methods follow reference [20] ('Most methods were identical to those described in detail recently [20]'), which places background ROIs 'near the poles outside of the cell' with no distance. The data check shows the membrane's glow is still a third of its excess 2 um out and a few percent 8 um out. The near (2 to 4 um) and no-background readings are shown and change dF by up to a factor of three. After verification round 1 every claim also shows a sweep of 6-pixel bands from 8 to 44 pixels out and a per-pole (local) background.

The perimeter trace (6 pixels wide, Methods 2.3) is found automatically as the peak of intensity on 360 rays of each set's baseline image, with polar angles from the cell centre; the paper drew it by hand in MetaMorph and resampled by perimeter length. Sets whose outline radius departs from the cell's median by more than 15% are traced again within 8 pixels of the cell's median centre and 4 pixels of its median radius; this re-traced FluoVolt c2 at 300 V (outline on a neighbouring cell) and Di-8-ANEPPS c7 at 300 and 350 V (outline on a body inside the cell), found in the outline overlays added after verification round 1.

Frames without a laser flash, which the files do not flag (frame 0 of 137 of 141 sets and 290 others), are left out of every average; the paper does not mention them. Keeping them is shown as a variant.

The field direction is not stored. The cathode-facing pole is placed where dF is positive (Methods 2.3, emission increased in the cathode-facing hemisphere), on one axis for all sets estimated from the 50 to 100 V sets (per-set median deviation 1.6 degrees).
All eight Di-8-ANEPPS escalation cells (c7 to c14) are used where the paper reports n = 5 without naming them; the criterion is also run on each of the 56 five-cell subsets.
Di-8-ANEPPS c13 has two 150 V sets; the first, in escalation order, is used.

outcomes.statement: With FluoVolt, pole dF rose with field strength until it saturated at 66% (255 mV) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole and -83% (-320 mV) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole; stronger fields did not increase the anodic response and decreased the cathodic one.
outcomes.quote: ΔF increased proportionally to the electric field strength until reaching apparent saturation at 66% ΔF (255 mV IMP) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole, and −83% ΔF (−320 mV IMP) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole. Further escalation of the electric field strength did not increase the dye response at the anodic pole and even decreased it at the cathodic pole.
outcomes.notes: Changed from partially_reproduced after verification round 1: the criterion requires both values, and both miss under the adopted far background. Per-image pole dF over the 60 pulse images, mean of 4 cells, far background: cathodic at 360 V/cm 49.4% against 66 +- 6.6, anodic at 570 V/cm -69.8% against -83 +- 8.3. The shape conditions hold (cathodic 48.1 and 37.4% at 570 and 780 V/cm; anodic -72.2 to -61.9% from 780 to 1400 V/cm; cathodic 36.6, 38.2 and 40.9% at 1000 to 1400 V/cm). Near 78.5 and -88.6% (anodic within, but 1400 V/cm rises to 80.4%, failing the 1000 to 1400 V/cm condition); none 23.7 and -37.6%. In the background sweep the band 14 to 20 pixels (4 to 5 um) out meets every condition (61.3 and -78.1%), where the membrane glow is still about a sixth of its excess; no band from 20 pixels out does. With c5 added, 55.2 and -71.2% (far); with dark frames kept, 45.6 and -69.8%.

outcomes.statement: FluoVolt measurements were stable without pulses (no significant bleaching or photosensitization), and the response within each set stayed stable through the 60 pulses, even at 1000 V/cm and above.
outcomes.quote: Without PEF (first 40 datapoints, or ~ 7 s in each set), measurements were stable, indicating no significant photosensitization or dye bleaching ... but the dye response in each set stayed stable through the 60 pulses applied
outcomes.notes: Claim of absence, 2-tailed paired t-test over 4 cells, 24 tests per reading (6 pulse comparisons at 1000 to 1400 V/cm and 18 baselines). Far background, reading (a) first and last image, 1 pulse set (1400 V/cm anodic, -3.2% dF, p = 0.043) and 1 baseline (1000 V/cm anodic, -7.0%, p = 0.005) change; reading (b) first and last 10 images, 2 pulse sets (1200 V/cm cathodic +5.5%, p = 0.049; 1400 V/cm anodic +2.5%, p = 0.037) and 3 baselines (150 V/cm cathodic -3.9%, 360 V/cm anodic +3.7% and cathodic -4.2%, p 0.000 to 0.008). Both readings find changes, so not reproduced. Without background both readings also find changes; with the near background reading (a) finds none and (b) three, so under that background the claim would be blocked as methods_underspecified. In the sweep reading (b) finds 3 to 6 changes at every distance. With 24 tests about 1.2 are expected below p = 0.05 by chance, and at least one in about 70% of stable recordings; the changes are a few percent dF (largest 7.0%) against responses of 40 to 70%. Whether the criterion should correct for the number of tests is asked of a reader in questions/001517.yaml.

outcomes.quote: This dye has a lower sensitivity to membrane polarization (note the vertical scale different from Fig. 2A), but ΔF kept climbing up to the electric field strength of 570 V/cm at both cell poles.

outcomes.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS responses were somewhat affected by bleaching, most visibly at 43 V/cm, where bleaching added about 5% to dF at the anodic pole and took about 5% from it at the cathodic pole.
outcomes.quote: The responses were somewhat affected by dye bleaching (particularly noticeable at 43 V/cm, where bleaching added ~5% to ΔF at the anodic pole and reduced it by the same ~5% at the cathodic pole.
outcomes.notes: Reading (b), the offset common to both poles in the 43 V/cm set, is -5.11% (far) and -5.00% (near), within -5 +- 0.5; without background -2.63%. Every band of the sweep gives -4.58 to -5.12% (within), the far local background -5.32% (within), the near local -6.30% (outside). Reading (a), last 10 minus first 10 pulse images, misses at the anodic pole under every background (far cathodic -5.32, anodic -3.39%). The result is fragile: 38 of 56 five-cell subsets pass under the far background (13 near, 0 none), and with dark frames kept reading (b) gives -2.18% (far). Over the last 10 pulse images both poles sit 7.2% below baseline (far), a downward drift through the set at both poles, as the text describes.

outcomes.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS, responses to pulses of 780 V/cm and above decreased gradually within each set of 60 images.
outcomes.quote: In addition, responses to PEFs at and above 780 V/cm decreased gradually in each set of 60 images, consistent with expectations of adding membrane damage by additional electroporation pulses in each set
outcomes.notes: Far background, cathodic |dF| from start to end of each set, reading (a) 40.1 to 35.8, 40.8 to 22.4, 32.2 to 17.4, 16.4 to 8.7% at 780 to 1400 V/cm; reading (b) 41.1 to 34.3, 37.0 to 25.2, 25.5 to 15.3, 15.6 to 8.7% (paired p 0.017, 0.001, 0.002, 0.092). Both readings decline in every set under every band of the sweep, without background and with the near background; with the near local background reading (a) fails. Five-cell subsets passing 44 (a) and 52 (b) of 56. The anodic variant does not decline at 780 V/cm. Bleaching control (after verification round 1): below electroporation the cathodic dF also falls through each set (reading b, -3.5 to -4.6% at 230 to 570 V/cm, common-mode change of both poles -1.7 to -3.4%), so the fall at 780 V/cm (-6.8%, -3.3% net of the common mode against -2.6% at 570) is about the size of the bleaching drift; the falls at 1000 to 1400 V/cm (-9.5 to -11.8%, net -6.0 to -7.5%) exceed it. The criterion holds as written; the part at 780 V/cm cannot be told from bleaching.

outcomes.statement: Fitted linearly through the origin over -150 to +150 mV IMPC, FluoVolt changes by 26% and Di-8-ANEPPS by 9.1% dF per 100 mV, with correlation coefficients 0.96 and 0.78.
outcomes.quote: The correlation coefficients of the fits equaled 0.96 for FluoVolt and 0.78 for Di-8 ANEPPS (due to a lower signal-to-noise ratio), with respective slope coefficients of 26% and 9.1% ΔF per 100 mV of IMP.
outcomes.notes: Changed from not_reproduced after verification round 1: two of the four values (the correlations) are within tolerance and the slopes are present but 17 and 19% lower. Far background, perimeter radius, slopes 21.57 (FluoVolt, 3008 points) and 7.38% per 100 mV (Di-8-ANEPPS, 5776 points) against 26 +- 2.6 and 9.1 +- 0.91; Pearson r 0.964 and 0.762, uncentred 0.950 and 0.660; ratio of the slopes 2.92 against the paper's 2.86. The equal-area radius gives 21.62 and 7.48. Near 30.69 and 11.46, none 10.95 and 3.33. With the pixel that gives the paper's average radius of 8 um (0.192 um) the far background gives 26.62 and 9.53 with Pearson 0.976 and 0.831, all within tolerance, as are the bands from 26 to 44 pixels; with the adopted pixel only the 14 to 20 pixel band passes (25.24 and 8.86). The files store no pixel size (the dump of a file in the data check holds no ImagingPlane, Device or grid spacing). With the field proportional to the volts the slopes are 13.05 and 4.37 (adopted pixel) or 18.03 and 6.00 (8-um pixel). Di-8-ANEPPS slope over the 56 five-cell subsets 6.48 to 8.27. The local backgrounds break down on whole profiles (Pearson 0.012 to 0.137 with the adopted pixel, 0.005 and -0.02 with the 8-um pixel).

outcomes.statement: Repeated alternating sets at 150 and 230 V/cm (480 pulses and 800 flashes) gave dF responses constant within and between sets.
outcomes.quote: Repeated sets of PEFs at 150 and 230 V/cm, delivered in alternation, produced ΔF responses that stayed constant both within each set and between the sets (Fig. 2C and D).

outcomes.statement: With 0.3-us pulses at higher fields (357 to 3320 V/cm), imaged at 275 ns, the maximum dF was 53 +- 4% (about 600 mV) at both poles, as with 1-us pulses, and the response changed with field strength in the same way.
outcomes.quote: Contrary to the expectations, the results were similar to those with 1-μs pulses in Fig. 4B: the maximum ΔF reached was 53 ± 4% (~600 mV) at both cell poles. The pattern of how the response changed with increasing PEF strength was not different from that with 1-μs PEFs either.

The paper says its data are available on request; the only other dandiset naming the paper, 001518, is by its title and description a FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS comparison at varying field strengths, and its files were not read.

outcomes.statement: With 1 mM Gd3+ the anodic pole charged to -864 +- 44 mV, against -542 +- 57 mV in parallel controls (p < 0.001).
outcomes.quote: Indeed, we found that 1 mM Gd3+ extended the range of membrane charging at the anodic pole down to −864 ± 44 mV (p < 0.001 compared to −542 ± 57 mV in parallel control experiments, Fig. 5A).
outcomes.notes: No set mentions Gd3+, and there is no group of parallel controls; the Fig. 5A data are not in the dandiset. The paper says its data are available on request; the only other dandiset naming the paper, 001518, is by its title and description a FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS comparison at varying field strengths, and its files were not read.

outcomes.statement: With Gd3+, the measured IMP stayed nearly identical to IMPC down to -780 mV, so the Di-8-ANEPPS calibration holds at high IMPs.
outcomes.quote: Furthermore, measured IMP remained nearly identical to the theoretical IMPC down to −780 mV, indicating that the dye response remained linear and its calibration was valid even at high IMPs.
outcomes.notes: The Gd3+ cells of Fig. 5A are not in the dandiset. The paper says its data are available on request; the only other dandiset naming the paper, 001518, is by its title and description a FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS comparison at varying field strengths, and its files were not read.

outcomes.quote: At the cathodic pole, polarization in the presence of Gd3+ reached 647 ± 44 mV, a value not significantly higher than that in the control group without Gd3+. However, Gd3+ prevented the progressive decline in IMP as the electric field was increased.
outcomes.notes: The Gd3+ cells and parallel controls of Fig. 5A are not in the dandiset. The paper says its data are available on request; the only other dandiset naming the paper, 001518, is by its title and description a FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS comparison at varying field strengths, and its files were not read.

outcomes.quote: Differences between Gd3+ and control group data are significant at p < 0.05 or better (2-tailed t-test) for datapoints below −700 mV and above 1200 mV.
outcomes.notes: The Gd3+ cells and parallel controls of Fig. 5A are not in the dandiset. The paper says its data are available on request; the only other dandiset naming the paper, 001518, is by its title and description a FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS comparison at varying field strengths, and its files were not read.

outcomes.quote: For most datapoints, Gd3+ reduced the electroporation- induced effective conductivity 2–3-fold.
outcomes.notes: Uses the Fig. 5A Gd3+ and control datapoints, which are not in the dandiset (it also depends on fig5b-conductivity-calibration, which was tested). The paper says its data are available on request; the only other dandiset naming the paper, 001518, is by its title and description a FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS comparison at varying field strengths, and its files were not read.

outcomes.statement: A single 1-us pulse caused clear Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 V/cm, with the signal elevated through 5 min; the small rise at 780 V/cm was not significant.
outcomes.quote: Exposure to a single 1-μs pulse at escalating field strengths, from 0 to 1200 V/cm established a clear peak of Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 V/ cm, and Ca2+ signal remained elevated through the 5-min observation period (Fig. 6A). A subtle ΔF increase after exposure at 780 V/cm was at the detection limit and not statistically significant.
outcomes.notes: The Fluo-4 Ca2+ imaging of Fig. 6A is not in the dandiset, which holds strobe images only. The paper says its data are available on request; the only other dandiset naming the paper, 001518, is by its title and description a FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS comparison at varying field strengths, and its files were not read.

outcomes.statement: After a train of sixty 1-us pulses at 6 Hz, 28% of cells responded strongly at 780 V/cm and nearly all at higher field strengths.
outcomes.quote: A strong Ca2+ response was recorded in 28% of cells exposed at 780 V/cm and in nearly all cells at higher intensities (Fig. 6B).
outcomes.notes: The Fluo-4 Ca2+ imaging of Fig. 6B (224 cells) is not in the dandiset. The paper says its data are available on request; the only other dandiset naming the paper, 001518, is by its title and description a FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS comparison at varying field strengths, and its files were not read.

outcomes.statement: At 650 V/cm only 2 cells (5.9%) responded strongly, yet the mean Ca2+ signal at the end of recording differed from zero (p < 0.001) and was marginally higher than at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05).
outcomes.quote: At 650 V/cm, only 2 cells (5.9%) showed a strong response, but the mean Ca2+ signal by the end of recording was significantly different from zero (p < 0.001, one sample t-test) and marginally higher than after exposure at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05, single-tailed t-test).

outcomes.notes: The Fluo-4 Ca2+ imaging of Fig. 6B is not in the dandiset. The paper says its data are available on request; the only other dandiset naming the paper, 001518, is by its title and description a FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS comparison at varying field strengths, and its files were not read.

outcomes.statement: A 150 V/cm test pulse 5 us after the conditioning pulse charged the poles as in undamaged cells after conditioning up to 760 V/cm, to about 80% (not significant) after 1000 V/cm, and to about 70% and 50% after 1200 and 1400 V/cm, a persistent permeabilization.
outcomes.source: Figure 7A and 7B, bottom panels; Results 3.7, paragraphs 3 and 5
outcomes.quote: Polarization still followed a cosine function after conditioning PEFs of up to 1000 V/cm. However, 1200 and 1400 V/cm conditioning PEFs markedly hindered charging by the test pulse at cell poles, indicating a persistent membrane permeabilization ... In contrast, measurements 6 μs later (test pulse) did not differ from the control up to 760 V/cm strength of the conditioning PEF; they were at ~80% of the control reading after 1000 V/cm conditioning PEF but the difference was not statistically significant. Still more intense PEFs of 1200 and 1400 V/cm reduced charging by the test pulse to ~70% and ~ 50%, respectively (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01, two-sided t-test).

statistics.about: 1200 V/cm conditioning, test pulse against control
1400 V/cm conditioning, test pulse against control

outcomes.notes: Every file states a single pulse; the two-pulse experiments with a 150 V/cm test pulse (Fig. 7A) are not in the dandiset. The paper says its data are available on request; the only other dandiset naming the paper, 001518, is by its title and description a FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS comparison at varying field strengths, and its files were not read.

outcomes.statement: Within 6 us of the electroporating pulse, effective membrane conductivity at the poles fell by a factor of about 10 (range 7 to 20) for most datapoints; the cathodic pole, more conductive during the pulse, no longer differed from the anodic pole at the test pulse.
outcomes.quote: Fig. 7C shows a profound reduction in the λm,eff within just 6 μs after the electroporating pulse. For most datapoints, it dropped by a factor of 10 (range: 7–20). While the cathodic pole became more conductive than the anodic pole during the electroporating pulse ... no difference between the poles was detected by the test pulse.
outcomes.notes: Needs the test-pulse data of Fig. 7A/B, which are not in the dandiset (depends on fig7ab-test-pulse-recovery). The paper says its data are available on request; the only other dandiset naming the paper, 001518, is by its title and description a FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS comparison at varying field strengths, and its files were not read.

outcomes.statement: After mildly electroporating 570 and 760 V/cm pulses the membrane resealed fully within 6 us; after stronger pulses a residual conductivity increase persisted.
outcomes.quote: For mildly electroporating PEFs of 570 and 760 V/cm, membrane resealed fully (within the accuracy of measurements) within just 6 μs. With more intense PEFs, the residual increased conductivity persisted for at least 6 μs, indicating the formation of more stable membrane lesions.
outcomes.notes: Needs the test-pulse data of Fig. 7A/B, which are not in the dandiset (depends on fig7ab-test-pulse-recovery). The paper says its data are available on request; the only other dandiset naming the paper, 001518, is by its title and description a FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS comparison at varying field strengths, and its files were not read.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only the 1-us escalation strobe images (6 FluoVolt and 13 Di-8-ANEPPS cells). The alternating 150/230 V/cm sets of Fig. 2C/D, the 0.3-us pulses of Fig. 4D, the Gd3+ cells and controls of Fig. 5A, the Ca2+ imaging of Fig. 6 and the two-pulse experiments of Fig. 7 are not in it; 15 of the paper's 31 claims cannot be tested.

The pulse amplitude is given only as generator volts inside a free-text session description (25 to 350 V). The paper reports field strengths in V/cm from Sim4Life modelling (43 to 1400 V/cm), which are not proportional to the volts, and no file or dandiset field gives the conversion; the nine steps had to be matched in order.

The files hold raw images only: each holds one ImageSeries with the frames, their rate and a general description, and no ImagingPlane, Device, field of view or grid spacing. The pixel size, the field direction, the cell outline or ROIs, and which frames are baseline and which carry the pulse are not stored; the 40/60 split is stated in the paper and is consistent with the data.
Every session description gives an electrode distance of 1.00 mm; the paper (Methods 2.2) and its reference [20] give 1.6 mm.
The dandiset description says Di-8-ANEPPS was used, replacing FluoVolt, but 68 of the 220 sets (6 cells) are stated in their session descriptions to be FluoVolt.

Frame 0 of 137 of 141 sets examined and 290 further frames hold no laser flash (frame mean near the camera floor) and are not flagged. Apart from frame 0 they are five times as frequent among pulse frames (257 of 8460) as among baseline frames (33 of 5499). Averaging them in changes dF by several percent (the Di-8-ANEPPS 43 V/cm offset goes from -5.1 to -2.2%).

The dandiset has eight Di-8-ANEPPS cells with the nine-step escalation where Fig. 2B and 4B report n = 5, five FluoVolt cells with it (one with an extra 350 V set first) and a sixth with a finer escalation where Fig. 2A and 4A report n = 4, and five Di-8-ANEPPS cells recorded on 2025-01-22 with other steps that the paper does not describe. Which cells the paper used is not stated.

Question for the authors. Where were the background ROIs of the strobe images placed, and how far from the membrane? Reference [20] says near the poles outside the cell. Here a background 2 to 4 um out, 8 to 10 um out, or none changes the pole dF by up to a factor of three (FluoVolt cathodic at 360 V/cm 78.5, 49.4 and 23.7%), and the 8 to 10 um reading was assumed. A sweep of 6-pixel bands from 8 to 44 pixels out shows the band 14 to 20 pixels (4 to 5 um) out would bring the FluoVolt saturation values, both Fig. 3 slopes and the first-10 Di-8-ANEPPS maximum within the paper's values.

Question for the authors. What is the pixel size of the images, and how was the cell radius measured? With 16-um camera pixels behind the 60x objective (0.267 um) the cells have mean radii of 7.8 to 15.1 um, larger than the 8 um the paper gives as typical, and the dye slopes of Fig. 3 come out 21.6 and 7.4% per 100 mV; with 0.192 um (radius 8 um) they come out 26.6 and 9.5, as in the paper.

Question for the authors. Which generator amplitude in the files corresponds to each field strength of the paper (is 25 V the 43 V/cm set, and so on), and which cells form the n = 4 FluoVolt and n = 5 Di-8-ANEPPS groups of Fig. 2 and 4? Both were assumed here (amplitudes matched in order; four FluoVolt cells with exactly nine sets; all eight Di-8-ANEPPS cells, with the 56 five-cell subsets shown).

Results 3.5 says a 10-fold rise of the effective membrane conductivity reduces IMP by about 2%; Eq. (2) with the constants of Methods 2.3 gives 1.3% (a 2% reduction needs a 15-fold rise). The 100-fold value (12%) agrees with the equation.

entries.name: 001517-semenov-2026
entries.title: Membrane charging and electroporation imaged with strobe fluorescence (Semenov et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Semenov, Silkuniene, Silkunas, Pakhomova, Bixler, Ibey, Kochunov and Pakhomov (2026) on dandiset 001517, which holds raw strobe images of CHO cells loaded with FluoVolt or Di-8-ANEPPS and exposed to 1-us pulses of escalating amplitude. Pole polarization, its decline within and across sets, the dye calibration against the Schwan equation and the departure from linear charging are rebuilt from the images. The Gd3+, 0.3-us, two-pulse, alternating-amplitude and Ca2+ experiments are not in the dandiset.
